standard.title: Algorithms for Classifying Shapes
standard.description: design and create algorithms involving a sequence of steps and decisions that will sort and classify sets of shapes according to their attributes, and describe how the algorithms work
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can classify triangles, quadrilaterals and polygons by properties (from AC9M7SP02). Students have experience writing step-by-step instructions and using decision trees informally.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students design and describe algorithms (using flowcharts or pseudocode) that sort and classify shapes by their attributes.

nodes.label: Designing a classification algorithm
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students design a step-by-step algorithm (as a flowchart or decision tree) that classifies shapes according to their attributes.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a flowchart that correctly classifies triangles as scalene, isosceles or equilateral.
nodes.typical_width: Design and test an algorithm for classifying quadrilaterals; identify and fix errors when the algorithm misclassifies a shape.
wider: Design an algorithm for a broader polygon classification including regularity and convexity.
Compare two algorithms for the same classification task — which is more efficient? Which handles edge cases better?

response_modes.reason: Algorithm design requires explicit thinking about the order of decisions and what each branch tests. Students who write algorithms informally miss cases and produce ambiguous decision points.

nodes.hinge_reason: Students who design algorithms without an explicit decision-ordering scaffold produce algorithms with missing branches or ambiguous tests — these cannot be evaluated or described correctly in Node 2, since tracing an incomplete algorithm produces unpredictable outputs.
success_criteria: Produces a flowchart or decision tree that correctly classifies the target shapes.
Includes decision points with clear yes/no branches.
Tests the algorithm on at least two examples and corrects any errors.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Designing a broader polygon classification algorithm that handles regularity and convexity, and comparing algorithms for efficiency, is a rich computational thinking task — advancing students engage with algorithm design as a genuine problem-solving activity.

nodes.label: Describing and evaluating algorithms
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students describe in words how an algorithm works and evaluate its correctness by tracing through it with test cases.
nodes.minimum_width: Trace a given classification algorithm with two test shapes and describe each decision made.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate whether a given algorithm is correct, efficient, and handles all cases; identify and fix errors.
wider: Implement the classification algorithm in a simple programming language or flowchart tool.
Investigate the relationship between the number of decision steps and the number of categories — how does complexity scale?

response_modes.reason: Algorithm evaluation requires seeing both correct and incorrect algorithms to develop critical judgment. Students who only design algorithms rarely develop the ability to critique others'.

success_criteria: Correctly traces a classification algorithm with a test input.
Identifies at least one case where a given algorithm fails (if one exists).
Explains in plain language how the algorithm works.
